body:
Inflexion has agreed an investment in French nail care brand Manucurist through its Enterprise Fund VI. Paris-based Manucurist sells its products across more than 40 countries and will use Inflexion’s backing to accelerate international expansion, particularly in the US, as well as further retail, digital and marketplace growth. French publication L’Informé previously reported that Inflexion’s offer valued Manucurist at about €300m, with the firm beating Advent International and Verlinvest in the sale process.

Abry Partners has agreed to sell Nordic vertical software platform Confirma Software to Main Capital Partners, ending a seven-year investment during which Abry built the company from its inception through 29 acquisitions. Confirma now generates more than €104m of revenue and serves more than 25,000 customers across Sweden, Finland, Norway and Denmark. Abry, which manages $16bn, originally formed the platform with CEO Jarle Mørk in 2019.

Arcventis Health Partners has made a majority growth investment in Chicago-based Aligned Modern Health, with existing backer Harbour Point Capital retaining a meaningful stake. The healthcare platform operates 15 clinics and a telehealth business spanning more than 20 US states, and plans to use the new backing to expand nationally, broaden its clinical offering and grow its provider base.

Atlantic Street Capital has invested in Toronto-based GLP, a specialist HVAC distributor serving utility, telecom and industrial customers. The lower-mid-market sponsor said the deal would support GLP’s expansion into new and existing markets. GLP was founded in 1958 and provides HVAC equipment, parts and components alongside engineering and system-design services.

RS2 Healthcare Partners has completed an investment in precision medical-device manufacturer KMM Group, its first new platform investment since adopting the RS2 Healthcare name. The Boston-based sponsor has installed J Mark King as chief executive, while founders John Shegda and Eric Wilhelm remain involved in the business. Pennsylvania-based KMM manufactures complex, tight-tolerance components for medical-device customers and other specialist markets.
